correctness.rationale: For a depth-u additive-tree pair (a,b), the torus parameters are P=a+b and Q=dP+b, so c=P(dP+b-1). Since P>=u+2 and b>=1, the lower bound is d(u+2)^2, uniquely at (a,b)=(u+1,1). The additive tree has P<=F_{u+3} and a,b<=F_{u+2}; equality in P occurs only in the two consecutive-Fibonacci orientations, and the orientation with maximal b uniquely gives the stated upper knot. Substituting d=n-2u into this pairwise maximum and comparing M_{u+1}-M_u proves balance is optimal, with the sole n=3 tie. Exact enumeration through u<=12,v<=14 and n<=24 agrees but is only corroborative.
